thread:
Lina (PM): quick heads-up — opened PR #3421 to consolidate the 429/timeouts section in errref. goal: one compact example per platform + a short migration note for context-trim and stream fallbacks. pls review when you can.

Maya (Docs): ack. can we also add a tiny example for the case where streaming is interrupted and the client needs to resume vs fall back to non-streaming? those snippets keep getting lost in other pages. :clipboard: 

Dan (SDK): linking the SDK retry snippet I usually give: 

```js
// recommended exponential backoff + retry-after handling
const res = await client.generate({ prompt });
if (res.status === 429) {
  const wait = parseInt(res.headers["retry-after"] || "1", 10) * 1000;
  await sleep(wait + jitter());
  return client.generate({ prompt });
}
```

Dan (SDK): note — the above intentionally avoids infinite loops and resets KV cache for context-trim errors. we should call out that clients must trim local prompt before retrying if upstream error indicates "context_length_exceeded".

Eli (EngRuntime): FYI runtime will emit a clear code for stream-interrupt: "stream_interrupted" + metadata { partial_tokens: n }. can we add a tiny paragraph: when this happens, treat partial output as best-effort and either 1) retry non-streaming with same prompt or 2) resume from KV if you persisted it.

Maya (Docs): proposed sentence for that: "If you receive a stream_interrupted error (runtime), the response may include partial_tokens. For critical flows, retry the request in non-streaming mode after trimming the prompt density; for recoverable UX, append a recovery prompt using the saved KV cache." happy to polish.

Lina (PM): perfect. one more ask: update the migration note to include the new retry header behavior (we changed from Retry-After seconds to Retry-After-ms in some infra paths). Dan, is the SDK handling both?

Dan (SDK): SDK will accept both numeric seconds and millisecond values now; it checks length > 1000 to infer ms and normalizes. will add a small comment in the snippet.

Maya (Docs): ok i'm adding two short examples: JS and curl. also adding a tiny troubleshooting card: checklist to triage 429 spikes (burst vs sustained, pin model variants, check routing policy). short bullet list only.

Lina (PM): cool — can someone do quick link hygiene check? a few internal links in the old errref still point to /guides/context-trimming-v0 which is deprecated.

Eli (EngRuntime): i'll grep and provide a list. also flagging a runtime note: if you get concurrent 429s + stream_interrupted, prefer to route to a lower-capacity variant rather than aggressive retries. i'll add a runtime-side comment you can quote.

Maya (Docs): draft is up at https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/3421 — reviews welcome. small ask: mark as "docs-blocker" label if you think this is urgent for customer-facing KB.

Lina (PM): marking it docs-blocker. target for merge by EOD Friday.

deploy-bot: CI passed for docs build (link-check: 0 broken, lint: 1 warning).

Dan (SDK): will add the normalized-retry snippet before EOD and drop a one-line test case.

Lina (PM): thank you team — this should reduce customer confusion on 429/timeouts + streaming.
